minideed.title: MiniDeed
minideed.stand: A social app where every like was worth a penny to charity. My first startup, which I talked my way onto while I was an apprentice at Goldman Sachs.
proof: raised, all of it to charity

beats.say: It started in the basement prayer room at Goldman. Mehti prayed next to me every day, and one afternoon on the way out I asked how he was doing, just being polite. He heard it as a question about his startup and told me everything.
posts: The best thing I did at Goldman Sachs was talk my way onto

beats.say: The pitch fit in one line. You see a cause on social media and feel helpless because all you can do is raise awareness, so we made the awareness itself worth something.
posts: You ever see a cause on social media and feel helpless

beats.say: I was in the first year of my apprenticeship and had no idea what I was doing, so I kept showing it to people. The company was two co-founders, one engineer and me. I did users and support, worked out what to build next, and posted about all of it.
posts: never I thought I’d read minideed praise in another language
Having a lot of fun presenting @MiniDeed

beats.say: People started opening up about their mental health on it, and users told us it was the only app where they felt safe doing that.
posts: MiniDeed is really precious tonight

beats.say: By the end it had raised £26,000 across twenty-five countries, entirely through likes.
posts: This MiniDeed journey has been amazing

beats.say: Then the users started guarding it. Someone would post something a bit off, within the rules and outside the spirit of it, and other users would step in before we'd even seen it. Nobody asked them to. It felt incredible and it was also the ceiling, because we'd built a room that only fit one kind of person.
posts: Years before Simply Smashed I built a little app, and one day the users started throwing people out

beats.say: The part I got wrong was taking follower counts away. They felt toxic to us, and a lot of people left over it.
posts: We raised £26,000 for charity through an app where every like

beats.say: Donations still trickle through daily, years after we stopped touching it. I kept the mug.

posts.m: In love with my new desk
posts.alt: My desk with the MiniDeed mug on it.

simply-smashed.title: Simply Smashed
simply-smashed.stand: A smashed burger joint my brother and I started in the back of a flower shop. It became London's highest rated on Google.

beats.say: We didn't plan any of this. The pandemic shut my dad's restaurant while my parents were stuck in Bangladesh, and me and my brother had a kitchen and nothing to cook in it.
posts: I didn’t plan to build Simply Smashed
We sold burgers from the back of a flower shop

beats.say: My brother bought a £100 grill. A few weeks after we opened we borrowed a projector and a screen to show the Euros final.
posts: Three years ago, we borrowed a projector

beats.say: Order times went from 50 minutes to 8. It started with me, a coffee and 50 ethernet cables I had no idea how to install, at 8am on a bank holiday Monday.
posts: We went from 50-minute order times to 8 minutes
8am on a bank holiday Monday

beats.say: We made a lot of decisions that looked stupid on paper. We closed for the first week of Ramadan, which cost us 30% of the month's revenue, built a prayer space where more tables could have gone, and ran Sisters' Nights with no men allowed.
posts: Why we're closing our restaurant for the first week of Ramadan
The UK has a prayer space problem
We ban men from eating at our restaurant

beats.say: Then a landlord told us we had to sell beer. We said no and walked away from the site.
posts: The landlord had one requirement: sell beer

beats.say: We were vocal about Palestine and got review bombed for it, so we doubled down.
posts: We got review bombed for supporting Palestine
"You're the Palestinian burger guy, right?"

beats.say: Two teenage brothers recited the entire Qur'an from memory in nine hours and finished two seconds apart. Their dad brought them to us straight after, and in the run-up to Ramadan we fed huffadh for free.
posts: These teenage brothers just recited the entire Quran from memory
We gamified Quran memorization with burgers and milkshakes

beats.say: Somewhere in the middle of all this my face became a Ramadan meme, globally, without my permission. Fair enough.
posts: Yes. I am the face of that meme

beats.say: We'd missed an item on an Uber Eats order, so I hired a Boris bike and cycled it to the customer myself in five minutes. He took the bag and shut the door without a word. I stood there for a second like... cool.
posts: I once hired a Boris bike to deliver a missing chicken burger

beats.say: I left in January 2026. My brother runs it now, and runs it better.
posts: I've left Simply Smashed. After 2 years of building the highest rated

beats.say: In August IFG made a documentary about us, and made it as much about my dad as the burgers. It's the best telling of our story so far.
posts: Adil and the team did a brilliant job capturing the Simply Smashed story
80k in 24 hours with IFG

psk.title: Peruvian Street Kitchen
psk.stand: Peruvian chicken and rice, built around a green sauce I spent months failing to recreate. My brother runs it now.
proof: to sell out the first drop
from the first box to launch

beats.say: There was a Peruvian place near the office in my Goldman days that I couldn't stop thinking about, years after I'd left. PSK exists because of a green sauce it took me sixteen goes to get right.
posts: There's this lunch from my Goldman days I can't get out of my head. After 16 failed

beats.say: Simply Smashed meant walking into a market with smashed burgers on every corner and trying to rise above them. PSK was the opposite, because most people here had never tried anything like it.
posts: I'm building @PSK_UKI because I want to bring some new flavours
Proud to announce our newest food brand

note.txt: ai slop, i know. we just didn’t have pictures yet

beats.say: Our first box was leftover chicken and rice. The one we launched with took two months of obsessing.
posts: Left photo: Our first PSK box

posts.m: First look of Peruvian Street Kitchen
posts.alt: The first Peruvian Street Kitchen box, chicken and rice under green sauce.

note.txt: until we did. and it tasted as good as it looked

beats.say: We ran a stealth test before opening properly. Someone spent £100 trying to sabotage it, which I found hilarious, and a dad tried to buy from us five times in one week and we were shut every time.
posts: Someone spent £100 trying to sabotage my stealth launch
A dad tried to buy chicken and rice from me 5 times in one week

beats.say: Running burgers and rice boxes out of one kitchen is absolute chaos. I found that out the hard way.
posts: Running burgers and rice boxes from the same kitchen

draper.title: Draper
draper.stand: We run LinkedIn for founders and their teams. Me, Mustafa and Aaquib.
proof: new investment Cur8 Capital puts down to its LinkedIn

beats.say: For the last two years of the restaurant I was quietly advising Series A founders on their content on the side. Nobody knew. I was taking calls with YC founders between burger orders.
posts: I've been lying to you. Every time you saw me at Simply Smashed

beats.say: Those two years at the restaurant taught me more about building than any MBA could. Every decision I make at Draper now, I can trace back to something I learned in that kitchen.
posts: I built the highest rated burger joint in London. 4.9 stars, 3000+ reviews. Those two years
I was building an AI company between burger orders

beats.say: Content is product and product is content. I've said it maybe 200 times now. We took a burger joint to the top of London with zero paid marketing, just by documenting the mess of building it.
posts: Content is product. Product is content.

beats.say: Most AI content is garbage. It's LLMs copying other LLMs, and you can feel it when you're scrolling because it all sounds the same. Builders should be building, and AI should be documenting you cooking.
posts: Let's address the elephant in the room - most AI content is garbage
I've been using AI wrong this whole time

beats.say: The problem underneath it is older than AI. The best thinkers I know don't post. Their best ideas come out loud, to one person, after the meeting, and then stay in the room. I wrote that up properly as The Corridor.
posts: AI has scraped nearly the entire internet

beats.say: Mustafa brought a deep work system over from his old agency, with client calls stacked on Mondays and Wednesdays and the rest of the week kept for building. I thought it was a bit rigid, and it ended up doubling our deep work without adding an hour.
posts: We 2x'd our deep work without adding a single hour

beats.say: This is roughly how Mustafa and I split the work.
posts: I'm the leg. Mustafa's the arm

beats.say: You can open Claude today and start building in a field you know nothing about. I keep going the slow way instead, into fields where I've put the reps in. Twice now, and I'd do it again.
posts: I keep entering domains the slow way

beats.say: Nine months ago people called me crazy for these ideas, and now the industry has names for them, forward deployed content engineers and AI native services firms.
posts: they called me crazy for these ideas 9 months ago

clients.said: Draper is quietly becoming indispensable. That's the best compliment I can give.
Traced enterprise contracts directly to Draper, plus top talent reaching out to Sahl AI.
Something is working. You guys really tickled the algorithm there.

draper.ask: If you want us to run it for you, book a call.

bilal.title: Bilal
bilal.stand: An athan that tells you when to leave for jama'ah at your masjid, not when the prayer starts. Out since 11 September 2026 on phone, Mac and the TV in your kitchen.
proof: people on it before launch day
from the question to the launch

beats.say: It started as a question I posted in October 2024. In Muslim countries you hear the athan from the minaret and you get up and go to the masjid. On your phone it's one more notification you swipe away.
posts: if you hear the athan out loud according to Jama'ah times
when you hear the athan from minarets in Muslim countries

beats.say: Two weeks later we'd started testing it.
posts: started doing early testing of project Bilal

beats.say: The first version lived on the TV in my front room for the best part of two years. Somewhere in that it started getting me to jama'ah I'd have missed, at mosques two minutes away that I never knew were there.
posts: im so excited to ship project bilal man
I can’t believe how many more Jama’ah I’m catching because of Bilal

beats.say: It launched properly on 11 September 2026 with the jama'ah times of over 2,500 masajid, on your phone, your Mac and the TV. The athan goes off when it's time to leave, and it's free and stays free. An iPhone app is coming soon, and Android after that, iA.
posts: Introducing Bilal. Finally.
Bilal for Mac
Bilal for the TV and Echo Show

beats.say: Before I'd announced anything it was already going round WhatsApp groups, and it had 1,400 people on it in a couple of days.
posts: Even before launching bilal started being shared

beats.say: The logo is a masjid arch, left open for you. Before you knew the way, someone took you to the masjid, and somewhere along the way most of us got lost again. There's still a place for you in the jama'ah.
posts: introducing bilal's logo
before you knew the way

vibenasheeds.title: vibenasheeds
vibenasheeds.stand: An AI that composes a track, then strips the instruments out so what's left is vocals and daf.
proof: between the complaint and the fix

beats.say: I've been complaining about this for eight years, which is documented and slightly embarrassing.
posts: native deen dropped so many bangers
nasheeds have regressed so much man

beats.say: Every Muslim creator hits the same wall. You either use beats you're not comfortable with, or you post in silence.
posts: Every Muslim creator faces the same impossible choice

beats.say: So I built an AI that composes music and then removes the music from itself. It sounds like a weird extra step, but composing with instruments first is how you get something that actually sounds good.
posts: Side project of the week: I built an AI that composes music

lofi-muslim.title: Lofi Muslim
lofi-muslim.stand: Vocals and daf, no melodic instruments. I made them after 12-hour shifts at Simply Smashed and put them on YouTube, and I've been on a break from it since January 2026. Three of them are below.

beats.say: I started making nasheed beats because I couldn't find halal background music I actually wanted to put on.
The peak was a mate playing them in the background at his wedding.
In January 2026 I put out my last beat and took a break from it, indefinitely. It was a fun ride.
posts: This is going to be my last beat

tracks.n: The one that plays in the footer.
For when you need the room to settle.

simply-clo.title: SIMPLYCLO
simply-clo.stand: A clothing line. One Palestine collection, made in Bangladesh, then wound down properly.
proof: to sell out the first drop

beats.say: When I was seventeen I did a summer internship at Jack and Jones in Bangladesh and designed a few t-shirts that actually got printed. Eight years later I went back to make a hoodie with my uncle, a senior graphic designer in the clothing industry.
posts: FIRST SAMPLE CREATED WE ARE COOKING

beats.say: The Liberation Hoodie went on sale on 21 December 2023 with all profits going to Gaza, and it sold out in three hours.
posts: THE LIBERATION HOODIE 21.12.23

beats.say: Then I closed it. Bootstrapping clothing meant production delays at every single step, and I'd rather end something cleanly than let it rot.
posts: Fear of God's Essentials hoodie retails at £180

simply-foundation.title: Simply Foundation
simply-foundation.stand: A boarding school funded out of burger profits. Four huffadh so far.

beats.say: Our family had been quietly running a madrasah and boarding school for a couple of years before we said anything publicly about it. Children from underprivileged villages live and study there while they work towards their hifz, and we cover their tuition, meals and accommodation.
posts: For the last couple years our family has built our own madrasah

beats.say: In 2024 we launched it publicly as a charity, and the profits from Simply Smashed pay for it. Four huffadh so far.
posts: Proud to announce the public launch of our charity

dhikry.title: dhikry
dhikry.stand: Dhikr with your closest circle. Invite only, on iOS.
proof: public post about it, after a month of use

beats.say: This one has almost no build log. My family and I used it every morning and evening for a month before I said a word about it in public, and that was one post.
posts: dogfooding the Adhkar app

beats.say: It's a small app for remembering Allah with the handful of people you actually pray for, morning and evening, and there's nothing else in it.
It's invite only, so the way in is a code from someone already in a circle.
